# Instacart component guide

Use this guide to choose a component and learn its rules. Start from the **Need → Use** table, then read the entry for each component you use. Every entry below is the component's own source documentation, and every props table is read from its TypeScript types.

On a canvas, each component is `<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.<Name>">`. Write `class-name`, never `class`, and write each prop in the **On a canvas** column form (`was-amount`, not `wasAmount` or `wasamount`). A value that is not text (a boolean, a number, an object or a handler) goes in a `{{ }}` hole from `renderVals()`: `loading="{{adding}}"`, `amount="{{lemonPrice}}"`.

## Need → Use

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| The one main action on a view ("Add to cart", "Checkout") | `Button variant="primary"` |
| Another action ("Show all", "View more") | `Button variant="secondary"` |
| A quiet action beside a filled one ("Log in") | `Button variant="tertiary"` |
| Remove or cancel something ("Remove", "Cancel order") | `Button variant="danger"` |
| A strong action that must not read as the brand green | `Button variant="neutral"` |
| A call to action that goes to another page ("Start shopping") | `Button asChild` around an `<a href>` |
| A button that is busy while "Add to cart" is sent | `Button loading` |
| A compact icon-only action ("+" on a product tile, "Close") | `IconButton` with an `aria-label` |
| Go to another page, or a link inside a sentence | `Link` |
| A page, section or product title | `Heading` (with `as`) |
| Body copy, fine print, a product size ("12 oz") | `Text` |
| The label of a field | `Text as="label"` with `htmlFor` |
| Any money amount ("$3.99", "$0.42/oz") | `Price` |
| A sale price with the old price | `Price tone="sale"` with `wasAmount` |
| A deal tag with no amount ("Sale", "No markups") | `Badge tone="sale"` |
| A fact or status ("Out of stock", "Organic", "Delivered") | `Badge` |
| A single-line text field, or a search | `Input` |
| A yes/no choice that applies when the form is submitted ("Leave at door") | `Checkbox` |
| A setting that applies instantly ("Substitution alerts") | `Switch` |
| A person: the shopper, a customer, the signed-in account | `Avatar` |
| An icon beside text, or on its own with a label | `Icon` |
| The Instacart brand | `Logo` |
| A wait you cannot measure ("Finding your shopper") | `Spinner` |
| An item quantity (- 1 +) in the cart or on a product tile | `QuantityStepper` with a `label` ("Quantity of Organic Lemons") |

## Actions

### `Button`

A pill-shaped button that does something: adds, saves, sends, removes.

**When to use:** any action. Pick the variant by meaning:
- `primary` for the main action, such as "Add to cart" or "Checkout".
  Use **at most one primary Button per view**; if two actions compete, make
  the other one `secondary` or `tertiary`.
- `secondary` for other actions: "Show all", "View more".
- `tertiary` (outline) for a quiet action beside a filled one: "Log in".
- `danger` for an action that removes or cancels: "Remove", "Cancel order".
- `neutral` for a strong action that must not read as the brand green.

**When not to use:**
- To go to another page or URL: use `<Link>`. (For a call to action that
  navigates, such as "Start shopping", use `<Button asChild><a href>…</a></Button>`.)
- For an icon with no text: use `<IconButton>`, which requires an `aria-label`.
- For an on/off setting that applies at once ("Substitution alerts"): use `<Switch>`.
- For a vague label: write the verb that says what happens ("Add to cart",
  not "Submit" or "OK").

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `variant` | `neutral` `danger` `primary` `secondary` `tertiary` | `'primary'` | What the button means, not how it looks. `primary` (default) is the one main action on the view; `secondary` the grey alternative; `tertiary` the outline; `danger` destroys or cancels; `neutral` a dark, non-green action. |
| `size` | `size` | `sm` `md` `lg` `xl` `icon-sm` `icon-md` `icon-lg` | `'md'` | Control height: `sm` 36px, `md` 40px (default), `lg` 48px, `xl` 56px. The `icon-sm`, `icon-md` and `icon-lg` sizes are square (36 / 40 / 48px) and need an `aria-label`; prefer `<IconButton>`, which requires one. |
| `asChild` | `as-child` | `boolean` |  | Render the single child element instead of a `<button>`, with the button's classes and props merged onto it. Use it for a link that looks like a button: `<Button asChild><a href="/store/sprouts">Browse Sprouts Farmers Market</a></Button>`. |
| `loading` | `loading` | `boolean` |  | Busy. Shows a Spinner in place of any icon, sets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, and ignores clicks. The button keeps its label, its width and keyboard focus. Use it while "Add to cart" or checkout is being sent. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Button" variant="primary" size="xl" class-name="w-full" loading="{{adding}}">Add to cart</x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<Button size="xl" className="w-full" loading={adding}>
  <PlusIcon />
  Add to cart
</Button>
```

### `IconButton`

A round, square button with only an icon in it.

**When to use:** a compact action whose icon everyone knows, where a text
label does not fit: the "+" on a product tile, a "Close" in a dialog
header, "Remove from cart" on a cart row. Always pass `aria-label`.

**When not to use:**
- When there is room for words, or the icon is not obvious: use `<Button>`
  with the icon and a text label.
- To go to another page: use `<Link>`.
- For a decorative or status icon that does nothing: use `<Icon>`.
- For a quantity control (− 1 +): use `<QuantityStepper>`. Never build one from
  two IconButtons and a Text.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` (required) | `aria-label` | `string` |  | REQUIRED. What the button does, in words, because the icon cannot say it: "Add 1 lemon to cart", "Remove from cart", "Close". Name the action, not the picture ("Close", not "X"). |
| `size` | `size` | `sm` `md` `lg` |  | Square size: `sm` 36px with a 16px icon, `md` 40px with 20px (default), `lg` 48px with 24px. |
| `variant` | `variant` | `neutral` `danger` `primary` `secondary` `tertiary` |  | As Button: `primary` (default), `secondary`, `tertiary`, `danger`, `neutral`. |
| `children` (required) | the tag's content | `React.ReactNode` |  | The icon, as a child: `<PlusIcon />`. Exactly one, and no text. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.IconButton" aria-label="Add Organic Lemons to cart" size="sm">
  <x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.PlusIcon"></x-import>
</x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<IconButton aria-label="Add 1 lemon to cart" size="sm">
  <PlusIcon />
</IconButton>
```

### `Link`

Text that takes you to another page.

**When to use:** navigation, and nothing else: "Offers subject to terms and
eligibility" in fine print, a store name, "View more" to a full aisle, a
help article, a link in a sentence.

**When not to use:**
- **Never for an action that writes data** (adds to cart, places or cancels
  an order, saves, deletes, signs out): use `<Button>`. A link may be
  prefetched, opened in a new tab or followed by a crawler, so it must only
  ever read.
- For a big call to action that navigates ("Start shopping"): use
  `<Button asChild><a href>…</a></Button>`, which looks like a button but
  is still a link.
- For an icon with no text: use `<IconButton asChild>` with an `aria-label`.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `variant` | `default` `inverse` `subtle` | `'default'` | The colour: `default` link green, `subtle` the surrounding text colour, `inverse` for dark surfaces. |
| `underline` | `underline` | `always` `hover` | `'always'` | `always` (default) underlined, or `hover`: underlined only on hover and focus. |
| `asChild` | `as-child` | `boolean` |  | Render the single child element instead of an `<a>`, with the link's classes and props merged onto it. Use it for a router link: `<Link asChild><RouterLink to="/store/sprouts">Sprouts Farmers Market</RouterLink></Link>`. |
| `external` | `external` | `boolean` |  | The link leaves Instacart (another site or a PDF). Opens it in a new tab (`target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`) and tells screen reader users so. Add a visible icon as a child if the page needs one. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Link" href="/help/fees" underline="hover">See fees</x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<Text variant="caption">
  *Service and other fees apply. <Link href="/help/fees">See fees</Link>
</Text>
```

## Text and prices

### `Heading`

Heading: a real h1-h6 heading, with its look set apart from its level.

**When to use:** page titles ("Order groceries for delivery or pickup
today"), section titles ("Often Bought With", "Items to add next") and card
or product titles. `as` is required, so every heading has a level in the
page outline.

**When not to use:**
- Body copy, labels or fine print: use **Text**.
- Text that is only bold or big for emphasis, with no section under it:
  use **Text** with `tone="strong"`.
- A price: use **Price**.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `as` (required) | `as` | `h2` `h3` `h1` `h4` `h5` `h6` |  | The heading level in the page outline. REQUIRED: pick it from the page's structure (one `h1` per page, then `h2` for sections, `h3` inside them), never from how big you want the text. Use `variant` for the size. |
| `variant` | `variant` | `h2` `h3` `h1` `title` `display` | `'h2'` | The type role, set apart from the level. `display` the one big page title · `h1` · `h2` · `h3` · `title` a card or product title. Leave it out to get the role that matches `as` (h4-h6 get `title`). |
| `tone` | `tone` | `strong` `brand` `default` `inverse` | `'strong'` | The colour role. `strong` (headings are the darkest text) · `default` · `brand` · `inverse` on an inverse surface. |
| `asChild` | `as-child` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead, with Heading's classes and props merged onto it. The child must then be the right heading element itself. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Heading" as="h2">Often Bought With</x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<Heading as="h1" variant="display">Order groceries for delivery or pickup today</Heading>
<Heading as="h2">Often Bought With</Heading>
<Heading as="h3" variant="title">Organic Bananas</Heading>
```

### `Text`

Text: body, label and caption copy in one of the type roles.

**When to use:** running text, fine print and short labels. For example a
product size ("12 oz"), a delivery fact ("Delivery by 7:30am") or small
print ("Service and other fees apply.").

**When not to use:**
- A heading or a section title ("Often Bought With"): use **Heading**, so
  the page has a real h1-h6 outline. Bold or big Text is not a heading.
- A price ("$3.99", "$0.42/oz"): use **Price**, which formats the amount
  and labels a sale price for screen readers.
- A status tag ("Sale", "Out of stock"): use **Badge**.
- Navigation: use **Link**. A click target: use **Button**.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `variant` | `label` `body` `caption` `body-lg` `body-sm` `label-lg` | `'body'` | The type role: what the text IS, not the size you want. `body-lg` · `body` running text · `body-sm` · `caption` fine print, the 12px floor · `label` control or field text (semibold) · `label-lg`. |
| `tone` | `tone` | `strong` `brand` `danger` `default` `inverse` `muted` | `'default'` | The colour role. `default` · `strong` emphasis · `muted` secondary facts ("Delivery by 7:30am") · `brand` green brand text · `danger` an error message · `inverse` text on an inverse (dark in light mode) surface. |
| `as` | `as` | `div` `label` `p` `span` | `'p'` | The element to render. `p` for a paragraph, `span` inline, `div` for a block that holds other blocks, `label` to name a form control (pass `htmlFor`). Never a heading: use Heading. |
| `asChild` | `as-child` | `boolean` | `false` | Render the single child element instead, with Text's classes and props merged onto it (for example a router link styled as caption text). |
| `htmlFor` | `html-for` | `string` |  | For `as="label"`: the id of the control this label names. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Text" variant="body-sm" tone="muted">Delivery by 7:30am</x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<Text variant="body-sm" tone="muted">Available at 35 stores</Text>
<Text as="span" variant="caption">*Service and other fees apply.</Text>
```

### `Price`

Price: a formatted grocery price, with an optional "was" price and a
per-unit price.

**When to use:** every money amount a shopper reads on a product, in the
cart or at checkout: "$3.99", a sale ("$2.99", was "$3.99") and a unit
price ("$0.42/oz"). It formats with `Intl.NumberFormat`, so pass a number,
never a string with a "$" in it.

**When not to use:**
- Do not write a price as plain **Text** ("$3.99" in a Text): it loses the
  formatting, the sale styling and the screen-reader labels.
- A deal tag with no amount ("Sale", "No markups"): use **Badge** with
  `tone="sale"`.
- A sentence that mentions money ("$0 delivery fees on your first 3
  orders"): that is copy, so use **Text**.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` (required) | `amount` | `number` |  | The price to pay now, as a number in major units (3.99, not 399). |
| `currency` | `currency` | `string` | `'USD'` | The ISO 4217 currency code. |
| `locale` | `locale` | `string` | `'en-US'` | The BCP 47 locale used to format every amount. |
| `wasAmount` | `was-amount` | `number` |  | The original price before a sale. Shown struck through after the current price, and read by screen readers as "Original price", because a line through text is not announced. |
| `unitPrice` | `unit-price` | `UnitPrice` |  | A per-unit price shown after the price, for comparing sizes: "$0.42/oz". |
| `size` | `size` | `sm` `md` `lg` | `'md'` | `sm` on a dense product tile · `md` the default · `lg` the product page. |
| `tone` | `tone` | `sale` `default` | `'default'` | `default` · `sale` puts the current price on the deal-yellow highlight. Use `sale` when the item is on sale, usually together with `wasAmount`. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Price" amount="{{lemonPrice}}" was-amount="{{lemonWas}}" unit-price="{{lemonUnit}}" tone="sale"></x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<Price amount={3.99} />
<Price amount={2.99} wasAmount={3.99} tone="sale" />
<Price amount={4.99} unitPrice={{ amount: 0.42, unit: 'oz' }} size="lg" />
```

## Status

### `Badge`

Badge: a small passive tag that reports a fact about the thing it sits on.

**When to use:** status and attributes on a product, store or order:
"Sale", "Out of stock", "Organic", "Delivered", "Only 3 left". The word
carries the meaning; the colour only supports it. An icon may go first, as a
child.

**When not to use:**
- Anything a person clicks or taps. A Badge is NEVER interactive: no
  `onClick`, no link, no focus. For an action use **Button**; to go
  somewhere use **Link**.
- A price or a saving amount ("$3.99"): use **Price** (with `tone="sale"`
  for a sale price).
- A sentence or a heading: use **Text** or **Heading**.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tone` | `tone` | `neutral` `brand` `success` `warning` `danger` `info` `sale` | `'neutral'` | What kind of fact the badge reports. `neutral` plain information ("12 oz") · `success` good news ("Delivered", "Organic") · `warning` act soon ("Only 3 left") · `danger` a problem ("Out of stock") · `info` neutral news · `brand` an Instacart label · `sale` deals and savings ("Sale", "No markups"), the deal yellow. |
| `size` | `size` | `sm` `md` | `'md'` | `sm` (caption text) on a dense product tile · `md` (label text) elsewhere. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Badge" tone="danger" size="sm">Out of stock</x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<Badge tone="sale">Sale</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger">Out of stock</Badge>
<Badge tone="success"><Check weight="bold" />Delivered</Badge>
```

### `Spinner`

A turning arc that shows something is on its way.

**When to use:** a wait you cannot measure, for example "Finding your
shopper…" after checkout, or a list of stores that is still loading. Put a
short visible message beside it, and pass the same words as `label`.

**When not to use:**
- A button that is busy: use `<Button loading>`. It draws its own Spinner and
  sets `aria-busy`.
- Content whose shape you know (a product grid): show the layout with
  placeholder blocks instead, so the page does not jump when it loads.
- A wait with known progress (an upload): use a progress bar.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `size` | `sm` `md` `lg` | `'md'` | How big the arc is: `sm` 16px, `md` 24px (default), `lg` 40px. |
| `tone` | `tone` | `brand` `muted` `current` | `'brand'` | The arc colour: `brand` green (default), `muted` grey, or `current` (the surrounding text colour). |
| `label` | `label` | `string` |  | What a screen reader hears. Say what you are waiting for, in a few words ("Finding your shopper"). It is not shown on screen: put visible text next to the Spinner yourself. Default: "Loading". |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<div class="flex items-center gap-3">
  <x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Spinner" label="Finding your shopper"></x-import>
  <x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Text">Finding your shopper…</x-import>
</div>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-3">
  <Spinner label="Finding your shopper" />
  <Text>Finding your shopper…</Text>
</div>
```

## Forms

### `Input`

Input: a single-line text field.

**When to use:** any short typed value: an email, a phone number, a promo
code, a delivery address line, a search ("Search products, stores, and
recipes"). It has NO label prop: always pair it with a `<label htmlFor>`
(or, for a search with a visible icon, an `aria-label`). Help or error text
is a separate element linked with `aria-describedby`. Show an error with
`aria-invalid`, never with a class.

**When not to use:**
- An item quantity ("how many lemons"): use **QuantityStepper**. Never an
  Input with `type="number"` for a quantity.
- A yes/no choice: use **Checkbox** (saved when the form is submitted) or
  **Switch** (applies instantly).
- Text that cannot be edited and is not part of a form: use **Text**.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `size` | `md` `lg` `xl` | `'md'` | `md` (40px) a field in a form or a dense panel · `lg` (48px) a roomier form or the aisle and product page search · `xl` (56px, pill) the one big home page search. |
| `type` | `type` | `React.HTMLInputTypeAttribute` | `'text'` | The native input type, passed through ("text", "email", "tel", "search", ...). Never `"number"` for an item quantity: use QuantityStepper. |
| `aria-invalid` | `aria-invalid` | `true` `false` `grammar` `spelling` `boolean` |  | Marks the value as wrong. This is the only way to show the error style: the red border reads this attribute. Point `aria-describedby` at the error message so it is announced. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` |  | The field cannot be used and its value is not sent with the form. |
| `readOnly` | `read-only` | `boolean` |  | The value can be read, selected and copied, but not changed. It is still sent with the form. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Text" as="label" variant="label" html-for="promo">Promo code</x-import>
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Input" id="promo" auto-complete="off" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="promo-error"></x-import>
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Text" id="promo-error" variant="body-sm" tone="danger">This code has expired</x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<label htmlFor="promo">Promo code</label>
<Input id="promo" aria-invalid aria-describedby="promo-error" />
<p id="promo-error">This code has expired</p>

<Input size="xl" type="search" aria-label="Search" placeholder="Search products, stores, and recipes" />
```

### `Checkbox`

Checkbox: an opt-in choice that takes effect when the form is submitted.

**When to use:** a yes/no choice inside a form that the person confirms
with a button: "Leave at door" on checkout (applied when they tap "Place
order"), "Save this address", "I agree to the terms". Also several
independent picks from a list, and a "select all" box (`checked="indeterminate"`
when only some are picked). Ticking the box changes nothing until the form
is submitted. Pair it with a `<label htmlFor>`; there is no label prop.

**When not to use:**
- A setting that applies instantly when toggled, with no save button
  ("Substitution alerts" in account settings): use **Switch**. If the
  change is saved the moment it is flipped, it is a Switch, never a Checkbox.
- One choice out of several that exclude each other ("Delivery" or
  "Pickup"): use a radio group (this system has none yet; do not fake one
  with Checkboxes).
- A command ("Add to cart"): use **Button**.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `checked` | `checked` | `indeterminate` `boolean` |  | Controlled state: `true`, `false`, or `'indeterminate'` (a "select all" box when only some items are picked). Use with `onCheckedChange`. |
| `defaultChecked` | `default-checked` | `indeterminate` `boolean` |  | Uncontrolled starting state. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `on-checked-change` | `(checked: CheckboxPrimitive.CheckedState) => void` |  | Called with the new state when the person ticks or unticks the box. Store it in the form; do NOT save it to the server here. If the change must apply right away, the control is a **Switch**, not a Checkbox. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` |  | The box cannot be changed. Its value is not sent with the form. |
| `required` | `required` | `boolean` |  | The form cannot be submitted until this box is ticked. |
| `name` | `name` | `string` |  | The field name sent with the form. |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `'on'` | The value sent with the form when ticked. |
| `aria-invalid` | `aria-invalid` | `true` `false` `grammar` `spelling` `boolean` |  | Marks the choice as wrong (for example a required box left unticked). This is the only way to show the error style. Point `aria-describedby` at the error message. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<div class="flex items-center gap-2">
  <x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Checkbox" id="leave-at-door" name="leaveAtDoor"></x-import>
  <x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Text" as="label" html-for="leave-at-door">Leave at door</x-import>
</div>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<form>
  <Checkbox id="leave-at-door" name="leaveAtDoor" />
  <label htmlFor="leave-at-door">Leave at door</label>
  <Button type="submit">Place order</Button>
</form>
```

### `Switch`

Switch: an on/off setting that applies instantly.

**When to use:** a setting that takes effect the moment it is flipped, with
no save button: "Substitution alerts" or "Order updates by text" in account
settings, "Show prices per unit" on a list. The new state is saved in
`onCheckedChange`. Screen readers announce it as "on / off". Pair it with a
`<label htmlFor>`; there is no label prop.

**When not to use:**
- A choice that only takes effect when a form is submitted ("Leave at door"
  on checkout, applied by "Place order"): use **Checkbox**. If there is a
  submit button, it is a Checkbox, never a Switch.
- Several picks from a list, or "I agree to the terms": use **Checkbox**.
- A command ("Add to cart"): use **Button**.

The rule, both ways: applies instantly when toggled → **Switch**. Applies
when the form is submitted → **Checkbox**.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | `size` | `sm` `md` | `'md'` | `sm` in a dense list of settings · `md` everywhere else. |
| `checked` | `checked` | `boolean` |  | Controlled state: on (`true`) or off (`false`). Use with `onCheckedChange`. |
| `defaultChecked` | `default-checked` | `boolean` |  | Uncontrolled starting state. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `on-checked-change` | `(checked: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the new state the moment the switch is flipped. Apply the setting HERE (save it right away); there is no Save button. If the change should wait for a form submit, the control is a **Checkbox**, not a Switch. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` |  | The switch cannot be flipped. |
| `name` | `name` | `string` |  | The field name, if the switch also sits inside a form. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-4">
  <x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Text" as="label" html-for="sub-alerts">Substitution alerts</x-import>
  <x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Switch" id="sub-alerts" default-checked="{{yes}}" on-checked-change="{{saveSubstitutionAlerts}}"></x-import>
</div>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<label htmlFor="sub-alerts">Substitution alerts</label>
<Switch id="sub-alerts" checked={alerts} onCheckedChange={saveSubstitutionAlerts} />
```

### `QuantityStepper`

QuantityStepper: the "− 1 +" pill that sets how many of an item are in the cart.

**When to use:** an item quantity, wherever a shopper changes how many of
a product they want: a cart row, a product tile after "Add" was pressed,
the product page. Always pass `label` with the item's name ("Quantity of
Organic Lemons"). Set `max` to the store's limit when there is one.

**When not to use:**
- Never an `Input` with `type="number"`, a raw `<input>`, or a hand-made
  pair of IconButtons around a Text for a quantity: use this component.
- For a number that is not an item count (a tip, an apartment number, a
  rating): use `<Input>` with a `<label>`.
- Before the item is in the cart: show an "Add" `<Button>` (or the "+"
  `<IconButton>` on a tile), then swap in QuantityStepper once it is added.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` (required) | `label` | `string` |  | REQUIRED. The name of the whole control, read by screen readers. Name the item: "Quantity of Organic Lemons", not just "Quantity". |
| `value` | `value` | `number` |  | The count, when the parent owns it (controlled). Pair it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | `default-value` | `number` | `min` | The first count, when the stepper owns it (uncontrolled). |
| `onValueChange` | `on-value-change` | `(value: number) => void` |  | Called with the new count after each press of − or +. |
| `min` | `min` | `number` | `0` | The lowest count. The − button is disabled here. |
| `max` | `max` | `number` |  | The highest count, such as the store's limit per order. The + button is disabled here. No limit when left out. |
| `step` | `step` | `number` | `1` | How much one press adds or removes. |
| `size` | `size` | `sm` `md` | `'md'` | `sm` (36px buttons) on a product tile, `md` (40px buttons, default) in the cart and on the product page. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` |  | The whole control cannot be used: both buttons are disabled and the count is greyed. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.QuantityStepper" label="Quantity of Organic Lemons" size="sm" value="{{lemonCount}}" min="{{one}}" on-value-change="{{setLemonCount}}"></x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<QuantityStepper
  label="Quantity of Organic Lemons"
  value={count}
  onValueChange={setCount}
  min={1}
  max={12}
/>
```

## People, icons and brand

### `Avatar`

Avatar: a round picture of a person, with their initials when there is no
photo.

**When to use:** to show who someone is: the shopper picking an order
("Maria Lopez is shopping for you"), a customer in an order list, the
signed-in account in the header.

**When not to use:**
- A product picture: use a plain `img` in the product card. Products are
  not round and must not be cropped.
- A store or retailer logo tile: it is a rounded square with a border, not
  an Avatar.
- The Instacart brand: use `Logo`.
- An icon on its own: use `Icon`.

**Accessibility:** with a `name` (or `alt`) the avatar is one image with
that name, whether the photo or the initials are showing. When the name is
already written beside it, pass `alt=""` so it is not read twice.

The photo loads in the browser, so server HTML shows the initials first.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src` | `src` | `string` |  | The photo's URL. While it loads, or if it fails, the initials show instead. Any shape of photo is centre-cropped to the circle. |
| `name` | `name` | `string` |  | The person's full name, such as "Maria Lopez". It gives the initials ("ML") and, unless `alt` is set, the accessible name. |
| `alt` | `alt` | `string` | `name` | The accessible name, when it should differ from `name` (for example "Maria Lopez, your shopper"). Pass `""` when the name is already shown as text beside the avatar: the avatar is then decorative and screen readers skip it. |
| `size` | `size` | `sm` `md` `lg` `xl` | `'md'` | `sm` 24px (a dense list), `md` 32px (most rows), `lg` 40px (a chat or order header), `xl` 64px (a profile page). |
| `tone` | `tone` | `neutral` `brand` | `'neutral'` | The colour of the initials fallback. `brand` (Kale) marks the Instacart shopper; `neutral` (grey) is for customers and everyone else. |
| `children` | the tag's content | `React.ReactNode` |  | Optional fallback content that replaces the initials, such as an `Icon` with Phosphor's `User` when there is no name yet. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Avatar" src="{{shopperPhoto}}" name="Maria Lopez" tone="brand" alt="Maria Lopez, your shopper"></x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<Avatar src={photoUrl} name="Maria Lopez" tone="brand" alt="Maria Lopez, your shopper" />

<div className="flex items-center gap-3">
  <Avatar name="Sam Patel" alt="" />
  <span>Sam Patel</span>
</div>
```

### `Icon`

Icon: a sized, coloured wrapper around one icon from the icon set.

**When to use:** any icon in the UI. Put one of the exported `*Icon`
components (`ShoppingCartIcon`, `ClockIcon`, `MapPinIcon`...) inside it,
next to text like "Delivery by 7:30am", or on its own with a `label`.
Use only those exports (the list is in the Foundations/Icons story);
never draw an svg by hand.

**When not to use:**
- A clickable icon: use `IconButton` (it needs an `aria-label`) or `Button`
  with `size="icon-md"`. An Icon is never interactive.
- The Instacart carrot or wordmark: use `Logo`.
- A person or store picture: use `Avatar`.

Icons are always passed as children. Do not set the icon's `size` or
`color` prop, and do not add size or colour classes to the svg: choose a
`size` and `tone` here.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` (required) | the tag's content | `React.ReactNode` |  | One icon from this package's icon set, such as `<ShoppingCartIcon />`. Do not set its `size` or `color`: the Icon sets both. |
| `size` | `size` | `sm` `md` `lg` | `'md'` | `sm` 16px (beside delivery text), `md` 20px (inside buttons), `lg` 24px (standalone UI icons). |
| `tone` | `tone` | `strong` `inherit` `brand` `success` `warning` `danger` `default` `muted` | `'inherit'` | The colour. `inherit` takes the colour of the text around it, which is right inside a Button, Link or Badge. Use another tone only for an icon that stands on its own. |
| `label` | `label` | `string` |  | The accessible name, for an icon that carries meaning on its own (for example "Delivery time"). With a label the icon is `role="img"`. Without one it is decorative and hidden from screen readers, which is right when text beside it already says the same thing. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Icon" size="sm" tone="brand">
  <x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.ClockIcon"></x-import>
</x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
import { ClockIcon, Icon, MapPinIcon, Text } from 'instacart-ps-ds';

<Text>
  <Icon size="sm" tone="brand"><ClockIcon /></Icon> Delivery by 7:30am
</Text>

<Icon label="Store location"><MapPinIcon /></Icon>
```

### `Logo`

Logo: the Instacart wordmark or the carrot mark, drawn from the official
artwork in the brand colours.

**When to use:** wherever the Instacart brand itself appears: the site
header, a footer, a "Shop on Instacart" partner moment, a sign-in screen.

**When not to use:**
- A retailer or store logo ("Sprouts Farmers Market"): use `Avatar` with
  the store's image.
- A carrot as a produce or category icon: use `Icon` with Phosphor's
  `Carrot`. The logo is the brand, not a picture of food.

**Brand rules (brand/brand.md, Logo):**
- Use the full-colour logo (`tone="color"` or `"cashew"`) only on white,
  Cashew, Kale, photos or video. On any other flat colour, use
  `tone="white"` or move the logo.
- Never smaller than 20px tall (`size="sm"`).
- Do not recolour, stretch, rotate, crop, or add shadows or gradients.
  Give it clear space about equal to its height.

**Props** this component adds (it also takes the usual HTML attributes of its element):

| Prop | On a canvas | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `variant` | `mark` `full` | `'full'` | `full` is the carrot and the word "instacart". `mark` is the carrot on its own, for small square spaces (an app icon, a favicon, a tight header). Prefer `full` wherever it fits: it is the primary brand expression. |
| `tone` | `tone` | `color` `cashew` `white` | `'color'` | The colour version. Pick it by the background: - `color`: Kale text with the Lime and Carrot carrot. For light backgrounds (white, Cashew). The primary logo. - `cashew`: Cashew text with the Lime and Carrot carrot. For Kale or other dark backgrounds. - `white`: all white. For photos, or a background where the full-colour logo is not approved. For the `mark`, `color` and `cashew` look the same (the carrot keeps its colours). |
| `size` | `size` | `sm` `md` `lg` | `'md'` | Height: `sm` 20px (the brand minimum; never smaller), `md` 24px, `lg` 32px. |
| `title` | `title` | `string` | `'Instacart'` | The accessible name. The logo is `role="img"` with this name. Pass `""` only when the name is already beside it in text; the logo is then hidden from screen readers. |

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Logo" tone="color" size="md"></x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<header className="bg-surface">
  <Logo />
</header>

<div className="bg-surface-brand">
  <Logo tone="cashew" size="lg" />
</div>
```

## Icons

The icons are real exports of this system (Phosphor, Regular weight). Only these exist: on a canvas each is `Instacart.` plus its name (`Instacart.ShoppingCartIcon`), in code `import { ShoppingCartIcon } from 'instacart-ps-ds'`. Never draw an `<svg>` by hand. To use an icon that is not listed, a developer must first add it to `src/icons/index.ts`.

Put one icon inside `Icon` (or straight inside a `Button`, `IconButton` or `Badge`), and give the icon no props: the wrapper sets its size and colour.

`ArrowLeftIcon`, `ArrowRightIcon`, `ArrowSquareOutIcon`, `BasketIcon`, `BellIcon`, `CaretDownIcon`, `CaretLeftIcon`, `CaretRightIcon`, `CaretUpIcon`, `CarrotIcon`, `CheckCircleIcon`, `CheckIcon`, `ClockIcon`, `FunnelIcon`, `GiftIcon`, `HeartIcon`, `HouseIcon`, `InfoIcon`, `LeafIcon`, `ListIcon`, `MagnifyingGlassIcon`, `MapPinIcon`, `MinusIcon`, `OrangeIcon`, `PackageIcon`, `PercentIcon`, `PlusIcon`, `ReceiptIcon`, `ShoppingBagIcon`, `ShoppingCartIcon`, `SlidersHorizontalIcon`, `SlidersIcon`, `StarIcon`, `StorefrontIcon`, `TagIcon`, `TrashIcon`, `TruckIcon`, `UserIcon`, `WarningCircleIcon`, `WarningIcon`, `XIcon`

**On a canvas:**

```html
<x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.Icon" size="md"><x-import component-from-global-scope="Instacart.ShoppingCartIcon"></x-import></x-import>
```

**In code:**

```tsx
<Icon size="md"><ShoppingCartIcon /></Icon>
```

## Missing parts

This system has atoms only. When a screen needs a part that is not here:

1. **Compose it from atoms** and the classes in the README's class table.
2. **Name what it stands for** in a comment (`<!-- ProductCard (composed) -->`), so developers can swap in the real one.
3. **Never hand-build a control.** No styled `<button>`, `<input>`, `<select>` or `<a>`.

| Missing part | What to do until it exists |
|---|---|
| ProductCard, Card | A `div` with `flex flex-col gap-2 rounded-lg border border-border bg-surface p-4`, holding an `img`, `Heading`, `Price`, `Badge` and `Button`. |
| Tabs | A row of `Link` elements if each tab is its own page. Otherwise say the part is missing. |
| Radio group, select | Not built. Do not fake a one-of-several choice with Checkboxes. Say the part is missing. |
| Dialog, sheet, toast | Not built. Compose the frame from layout classes (`bg-surface rounded-lg shadow-overlay p-6`) and put real atoms inside. Mark it composed. |
